mechanism_narrative: A persistent week-on-week rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility signals tightening stay-at-home policy enforcement, which mechanically suppresses discretionary retail and recreation trips, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 5.9 to 12.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean rises above its last-28-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to increase week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls by more than 10 points week-on-week, this signals a new round of lockdown-style restrictions on movement, which will drag RETAIL_REC lower over the subsequent two weeks as fewer people travel to shopping and leisure destinations.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from -47.0 to -59.7 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean does not fall relative to the prior 2-week mean despite TRANSIT's sharp week-on-week decline.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sharp declines in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicate a coordinated restriction tightening (reduced commuting and transit use together), which compounds to suppress RETAIL_REC more strongly than either series alone would predict, over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall more than 8 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -17.7 to -29.9 and TRANSIT fell from -47.0 to -59.7 in the same week (t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean rises or remains flat relative to the prior 4-week mean despite the joint WORKPLACES/TRANSIT co-decline.

mechanism_narrative: In an essential-only mobility regime, GROCERY_PHARM declines much less than RETAIL_REC because grocery and pharmacy trips are necessity-driven and inelastic, while discretionary retail trips are cut first and remain suppressed; this gap persists as long as the regime holds, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell only from -6.7 to -10.1 while RETAIL_REC fell from -20.4 to -35.7 in the same week
failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC narrows (RETAIL_REC recovers toward GROCERY_PHARM's level) while the regime is still classified as essential-only, or RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility reflects reduced outdoor seasonal activity (e.g. weather or restricted outdoor gathering limits), which correlates with broader reductions in non-essential movement including retail and recreation trips, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -20.0 to -27.4 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean rises relative to its prior 2-week mean despite PARKS continuing to decline.

mechanism_narrative: The single-week RETAIL_REC drop of more than 10 points beyond its prior 3-week average represents a short-term shock (e.g. a one-off announcement effect or data anomaly) rather than a sustained shift, so mobility will partially mean-revert upward over the following week.
candidate_trigger: weekly RETAIL_REC drops more than 10 points below the prior 3-week average
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -20.4 to -35.7, a 15.3 point single-week drop versus a ~-20.3 three-week prior average
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat at the lower level for the next week rather than rebounding upward.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with falling WORKPLACES mobility jointly signal a behavioral shift toward sustained home-based routines (remote work plus reduced errands), and this combination has a compounding suppressive effect on RETAIL_REC beyond what either series predicts alone, over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 12.1 while WORKPLACES fell to -29.9 in the same week (t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean is higher than its prior 4-week mean despite the RESIDENTIAL-up/WORKPLACES-down co-movement persisting.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains below -55 percent change from baseline for a full week, this signals an active lockdown regime restricting non-essential movement, under which RETAIL_REC will stay suppressed or decline further over the next two weeks until the threshold is crossed back.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -55 for the week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -59.7 at t-0w, below the -55 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean rises above its prior 2-week mean while TRANSIT remains below -55.
